title: The Gravity of Station Meridian Anew
premise: Jonah Okonkwo keeps the beacon at Station Meridian Anew burning and keeps her head down, but the backups of massacre victims sleeping in her hold are a secret that will not stay buried. When a manifest for a ship that never flew surfaces with a name she buried years ago, Jonah is pulled into an investigation the fleet itself has erased, alongside a disgraced auditor and the station's ragtag found family. As the truce between fleet factions expires, she must broadcast proof of the Meridian massacre through the very beacon she maintains, knowing the signal will mark her for execution. She chooses justice over survival, and the ending leaves the truth loose in the dark, the family scattered but alive, and Jonah finally at peace with the ghosts she carries.
about_author: Ansel Yarrow is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade maintaining lighthouse beacons off the northern coast before turning to science fiction. Their work explores the quiet heroism of people who keep things running long after everyone has stopped looking.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Asked For
chapters.summary: Jonah Okonkwo's POV. She performs her lonely maintenance rounds on Meridian Anew's ancient beacon, establishing her routines, her isolation, and her habit of talking to the cryo-backups in the hold she officially isn't supposed to know about. Emotional beat: tender melancholy and quiet complicity.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. While filing routine cargo logs, she finds a manifest for the ship Vesperine, decommissioned before it ever flew, bearing the name 'Rhee Okonkwo'—her brother, dead nine years. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of a carefully ordered life.

chapters.title: The Auditor in Dock Nine
chapters.summary: New POV: Sef Ibarra, a disgraced fleet auditor exiled to the station, notices Jonah's query flags on the Vesperine file. He approaches her with careful, self-interested curiosity. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two people hiding things.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She opens the backup bay and confronts the truth: the sleeping backups are copies of massacre victims, smuggled aboard by her brother before he died. Emotional beat: grief transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Fleet bulletins announce the faction truce expires in ninety days; after that, records disputes become treason. Sef realizes the Vesperine file could redeem him—or destroy him. Emotional beat: ambition wrestling with conscience.

chapters.title: The Galley Parliament
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV through station cook Mirela Duval, matriarch of the station's unofficial family. The crew debates whether to help Jonah or report her. Emotional beat: found family choosing loyalty over safety.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, flashback-heavy. How her brother Rhee became a records clerk, what he suspected about the Meridian massacre, and why she let the world believe he never existed. Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: Erasure Protocol
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. He tests the fleet archive and finds the Vesperine's entire service history is a seamless fabrication—too seamless, made by someone with command authority. Emotional beat: the chill of institutional power.

chapters.title: The Passenger in Cryo
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. One backup begins waking early: a woman named Adaeze Voss, massacre survivor, disoriented and furious. Emotional beat: a ghost made flesh, demanding to be believed.

chapters.title: Contraband Truth
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. The family smuggles Adaeze through the station's public decks disguised as a dockworker. First brush with fleet security. Emotional beat: terror laced with exhilaration.

chapters.title: What Adaeze Saw
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Her testimony: the fleet ship Cassiopia fired on the refugee convoy at Meridian, and every surviving record was rewritten within the hour. Emotional beat: testimony as wound reopened.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. He traces the falsification to Commodore Lassiter Hale, the truce's chief architect, now a peace icon. Emotional beat: disillusionment curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: Beacon Physics
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She calculates that the beacon could carry a burst transmission to every ship in the sector—but only once, and it would burn out the array and her anonymity forever. Emotional beat: the shape of sacrifice becoming visible.

chapters.title: Ninety Minus Forty
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Fifty days to truce expiry. He requests a formal audit of the Vesperine, knowing it will summon Hale's attention to the station. Emotional beat: deliberately lighting a fuse.

chapters.title: The Family That Isn't
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. Quiet chapter: the crew shares a meal, and Adaeze is folded into the family's rituals. Jonah and Sef circle each other. Emotional beat: warmth as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: Hale Arrives
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV, hidden. Commodore Hale docks at Meridian Anew under a diplomatic pretext, all charm and medals. Adaeze recognizes his voice from the massacre broadcast. Emotional beat: the predator walking calmly through the henhouse.

chapters.title: Audit and Obfuscation
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. His audit hearing is a theater of stalling; Hale's aide offers him reinstatement in exchange for closing the file. Emotional beat: temptation with a knife in it.

chapters.title: Rhee's Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Decoding her brother's old cipher, she finds a hidden partition in the beacon itself: raw sensor logs of the massacre, Rhee's insurance policy. Emotional beat: a dead brother's hand reaching across years.

chapters.title: The Price of the Signal
chapters.summary: Jonah and Sef's alternating POV. The logs are corrupted without the cryo-backups' neural checksums to repair them. They must wake more of the sleeping. Emotional beat: using the dead as instruments, and the ethics of it.

chapters.title: Waking the Convoy
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Twelve backups wake; the station's medbay becomes a ward of the returned dead. One survivor recognizes Adaeze and breaks down. Emotional beat: communal grief as fuel.

chapters.title: Security Sweep
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. Hale's marines sweep the station hunting a 'stowaway.' The family runs interference, hiding survivors in the beacon's service shafts. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into competence.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Hale, having deduced who she is, offers her everything: her brother's record cleared, a new identity, the backups quietly deleted. Emotional beat: the seduction of a clean slate.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She refuses, and Hale gives her seventy-two hours before he takes the station apart. She tells the family everything. Emotional beat: the relief of having no way back.

chapters.title: Repairing the Dead
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The checksum reconstruction works; the massacre logs become whole and verifiable. Sef realizes the data is only half the proof—they need a living chain of custody. Emotional beat: hope that requires more courage.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. The survivors vote: broadcast or scatter? Adaeze argues for the beacon, for the dead, for the record. Emotional beat: democracy among the condemned.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. A family member—dockhand Piet, terrified for his kids—sabotages the beacon array for Hale's amnesty. Emotional beat: betrayal born of love, not malice.

chapters.title: The Long Night Shift
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. With hours left, Jonah and Sef physically repair the array by hand in vacuum, racing Hale's deadline. Emotional beat: two lonely people becoming partners under the stars.

chapters.title: Piet's Confession
chapters.summary: Piet's POV. He confesses to Mirela; the family does not cast him out but gives him the hardest job in the plan. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a load-bearing structure.

chapters.title: Hale's Peace
chapters.summary: Hale's POV, the only chapter from the antagonist. His logic: the massacre was a necessary price for the truce that saved a million lives. Emotional beat: the horror of sincere conviction.

chapters.title: Countdown to Dawn
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Final preparations: survivors wired in as witnesses, Sef drafting the broadcast warrant, Jonah at the beacon controls. Emotional beat: held breath.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The beacon fires the truth into every ship in the sector—massacre logs, testimony, Hale's own signature on the falsification order. The array burns out. Emotional beat: exaltation and dread in the same breath.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Hale orders the station seized and the witnesses 'decommissioned.' Marines breach the docks; the family executes the evacuation plan through the beacon shafts. Emotional beat: chaos held together by rehearsed trust.

chapters.title: What the Sector Heard
chapters.summary: Multi-POV montage: crews on forty ships receiving the broadcast, some ignoring it, some weeping, one destroyer's captain turning her guns toward Hale's flagship. Emotional beat: truth as contagion.

chapters.title: The Standoff at Meridian
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Hale's marines corner the survivors in the hold; Adaeze walks out unarmed and names the dead, one by one, while the marines' own ships relay her voice. Emotional beat: moral force against armed power.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Honest
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Three fleet captains, backed by the broadcast, demand Hale's surrender and a tribunal. Hale refuses; his own flagship's crew stands down. Emotional beat: the law reconstituting itself from below.

chapters.title: The Cost
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In the fighting, Mirela is killed shielding the cryo-bay. The family grieves in the burned-out beacon room. Emotional beat: justice priced in blood.

chapters.title: Tribunal at Dawn
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Hale faces a restored court; Sef testifies, reinstated and hollow. The verdict: guilty. The truce holds, rewritten on honest terms. Emotional beat: vindication that tastes like ash.

chapters.title: The Sleeping and the Waking
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. The surviving backups choose their futures—some stay, some ship out, some choose to sleep again until the war is truly over. Emotional beat: autonomy returned to the returned.

chapters.title: A New Commission
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The fleet offers Jonah the station permanently, with a rebuilt beacon and a crew. Rhee's name is restored to the record. She finally reads his last letter. Emotional beat: grief settling into gratitude.

chapters.title: The Gravity of Station Meridian Anew
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, closing. A year later: the beacon burns, the family gathers in Mirela's rebuilt galley, and Jonah keeps a small light burning for the backups still sleeping. Some gravity you escape; some you choose to orbit. Emotional beat: home as a decision, made daily.
